articles.title: NASA JPL Looks to Next 90 Years of Innovation, Exploration
articles.description: Interstellar probes. Lunar drones. Helicopters on Mars. When a group of Caltech graduate students and enthusiasts began conducting rocket-propulsion tests in Pasadena’s Arroyo Seco on Oct. 31, 1936, they had no idea that their work marked the inception of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory. Ninety years later, the lab, now managed by Caltech for NASA, isn’t […]
articles.summary: NASA JPL celebrates 90 years of innovation while unveiling ambitious visions including interstellar probes, lunar drones, and Mars helicopters. These breakthrough concepts represent the next frontier of robotic exploration and discovery.

articles.title: MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.description:
Image:
			MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission successfully launches toward Mars's intriguing moon Phobos. This pioneering mission will unlock secrets about the Martian system and planetary moon formation.

articles.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
articles.description:
Video: 
			00:03:32
				
BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. After eight years of travelling through the inner Solar System, the ESA/JAXA mission will arrive at Mercury on 9 December, 2026. To celebrate, mission team members were asked to describe BepiColombo in just three words.
Their answers capture the character of the mission and the people behind it. Complex, collaborative and transformative are among the words chosen, reflecting both the demanding journey to Mercury and the international teamwork that has made it possible. Together, their words offer a personal snapshot of BepiColombo as it approaches its long-awaited destination.
articles.summary: BepiColombo celebrates eight years of successful operation studying Mercury, marking a milestone anniversary for this groundbreaking ESA-JAXA mission. The spacecraft continues to reveal unprecedented insights into our innermost planet.

articles.title: Neutrinos May Be The Key To Why We Are Surrounded By Matter
articles.description: In the early Universe, neutrinos interacted strongly with other matter before some of them "decoupled." The heaviest of these decoupled neutrinos may be the solution to the matter-antimatter cosmic mystery.
articles.summary: Groundbreaking research suggests neutrinos may hold the key to explaining why the universe is composed primarily of matter rather than antimatter.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover just shattered the all-time off-world driving record
articles.description: NASA’s Perseverance rover has shattered a historic space exploration record, traveling farther across another world than any vehicle before it. Its advanced self-driving system helped it surpass Opportunity’s 28.06-mile record in just five and a half years, a feat that previously took nearly 15. Now, Perseverance is exploring some of the oldest rocks in the solar system, searching for clues about ancient Martian environments that may once have supported life.
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover has set a new record for off-world driving distance, surpassing all previous planetary exploration achievements. This milestone celebrates human engineering and the continued success of Mars exploration.

articles.title: Astronomers uncover new secrets of the Universe’s first five minutes
articles.description: Scientists have achieved a major breakthrough in understanding the Universe’s earliest moments, measuring the amount of helium formed in the first five minutes after the Big Bang with unprecedented precision. Using one of the world’s most powerful telescopes, an international team studied 15 remarkably pristine galaxies that act as cosmic time capsules, preserving clues from nearly 13.8 billion years ago.
articles.summary: Astronomers have achieved a major breakthrough in understanding the Universe's first five minutes through new measurements of primordial abundances. This discovery illuminates the earliest moments of cosmic history.

articles.title: NASA reveals 16 stunning galaxies hiding cosmic chaos
articles.description: NASA's stunning new gallery of 16 galaxies reveals colossal black hole jets, explosive star formation, and spectacular cosmic collisions through the combined power of Chandra, James Webb, Hubble, and other telescopes. These extraordinary images expose the hidden forces shaping galaxies across the universe and offer clues about the Milky Way's own past and future.
articles.summary: NASA's new gallery reveals 16 stunning galaxies featuring spectacular black hole jets, explosive star formation, and cosmic phenomena. These remarkable images showcase the dynamic and beautiful universe revealed by modern telescopes.

articles.title: SpaceX will attempt 1st-ever double Starship rocket catch on next test launch, a 'profound technology milestone,' Elon Musk says
articles.description: SpaceX will try to recover both Starship stages during the megarocket's next test flight, which is expected to take place in November, according to Elon Musk.
articles.summary: SpaceX plans to attempt a historic double catch of both Starship rocket stages during the next test flight, representing a profound technological milestone for reusable launch systems.

articles.title: IceCube, high-energy neutrinos, and Francis Halzen win 2026’s Physics Nobel
articles.description:
Back in 1988, Francis Halzen had what he called a “cute idea.” His vision grew into the IceCube observatory, and earns the 2026 Nobel…
Continue reading on Starts With A Bang! »
articles.summary: Francis Halzen and the IceCube neutrino observatory win the 2026 Physics Nobel Prize for breakthrough discoveries in high-energy neutrino astronomy.

articles.title: APOD: 2026 October 22 – The First Green Star, WD J1330+6435
articles.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 22 – The… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss   APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. The First […]
articles.summary: Astronomers discover WD J1330+6435, the first green star ever observed, revealing unprecedented stellar phenomena. This landmark discovery expands our understanding of stellar diversity and exotic stellar objects.

articles.title: Faster to Science: A Letter to the Science Community
articles.description: NASA Science wants to deliver science faster, so we’re changing how we compete and select missions. On Monday, October 26, we will host a virtual NASA Science Town Hall.
articles.summary: NASA Science announces streamlined mission competition and selection processes to accelerate scientific discoveries and get results to the research community faster. This structural reform promises to enhance innovation in space exploration.

articles.title: NASA Conducts RS-25 Engine Test in Support of Future Artemis Missions
articles.description: NASA tested RS-25 engine No. 10001 on Oct. 21 on the Fred Haise Test Stand at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi. Test teams fired the developmental engine for almost eight-and-a-half minutes (500 seconds), the same amount of time RS-25 engines fire during launch of NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket. During […]
articles.summary: NASA successfully tests RS-25 engine No. 10001 at Stennis Space Center, advancing propulsion technology for future Artemis lunar missions. This critical test validates engine performance for humanity's return to the Moon.

articles.title: Tracks Along the Longest Drive on Another World
articles.description: Written by Vandi Verma, Chief Engineer for Robotic Operations at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory Oct. 12, 2026 Since the last blog update, Perseverance has achieved a major milestone on Mars. On Sol 2006 (Oct. 11, 2026), its odometer reached 45.22 kilometers (28.10 miles), setting a new record for the farthest distance driven on another celestial […]
articles.summary: NASA celebrates a historic milestone with the longest drive ever completed on another world by a robotic rover. This achievement showcases the durability and success of Mars exploration technology.

articles.title: Science on the Space Station with NASA Astronaut Jessica Watkins
articles.description: NASA astronaut and Expedition 75 flight engineer Jessica Watkins works inside the Kibo laboratory module’s Life Science Glovebox on Oct. 9, 2026, safely mixing living cell samples with a bioink and then filling a special cartridge with the cell‑ink mixture. The advanced research operations were part of the InSPA‑Auxilium Bioprinter‑Cell Printing investigation, which explores 3D […]
articles.summary: NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins conducts groundbreaking life science experiments aboard the International Space Station in the Kibo laboratory module. Her work advances human knowledge of biology in microgravity environments.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope discovers its first previously unknown comet, demonstrating the mission's exceptional capability for detecting faint solar system objects. This discovery highlights the telescope's scientific potential.

articles.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
articles.description:
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. 
MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch on an H3 rocket toward Mars's moon Phobos, representing an exciting new chapter in Mars system exploration. This mission promises extraordinary scientific discoveries.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: The ESA Solar Orbiter spacecraft flies through a magnetic switchback in the solar wind, revealing new insights into mysterious magnetic structures near the Sun. This discovery advances our understanding of solar magnetic phenomena.

articles.title: Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
articles.description:
Image:
			Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captures dynamic stellar jets and outflows from a nebula, revealing the energetic processes of star formation in unprecedented detail.

articles.title: How Flare Ribbons Reveal Hidden Solar Explosions on the Sun
articles.description: Solar flaring is complex behaviour triggered by reconnection, when magnetic field lines break and then snap back to the Sun's surface. The flaring is complex behaviour, and its details are difficult to observe. Researchers found a new way to study flaring behaviour.
articles.summary: New research explains how solar flares and their characteristic ribbon structures form through magnetic field reconnection, advancing our understanding of solar dynamics.

articles.title: Webb Captures Stars in the Early Stages of Life in a Nearby Stellar Nursery
articles.description: This Webb infrared image, released on October 6th, 2026, shows the star-forming region NGC 7129, about 3,300 light-years from Earth. The central star, LkHα 234, is a young star of 5–8 solar masses whose outflows have cleared a cavity about 3.5 light-years across. On the right side of the region, younger protostars shoot jets of very hot material that create shocks in the surrounding gas.
articles.summary: Webb's infrared observations of NGC 7129 reveal newborn stars in their earliest stages of development, providing insights into stellar birth processes 3,300 light-years away.

articles.title: There Should Be Black Holes in our Neighbourhood. Can We Find Them?
articles.description: Stellar-mass black holes should be in our neighbourhood within about 50 light years of the Solar System. But they're  likely isolated, without much to feed on, making them difficult to find. Gaia found some candidates, but confirming them is tough.
articles.summary: Research investigates the possibility of discovering stellar-mass black holes in our cosmic neighborhood within 50 light-years, expanding our understanding of nearby compact objects.

articles.title: A Stubborn Question Answered: New Research Reveals How the Milky Way's Disk Formed
articles.description: Figuring out how the Milky Way's thin and thick disks formed is a tough question in astronomy. It relies on determining individual stellar ages accurately. Gaia was pretty good at that, and new research based on its data may have found the answer.
articles.summary: New research solves a longstanding astronomy puzzle by revealing how the Milky Way's thin and thick galactic disks formed through distinct evolutionary processes.

articles.title: How Inversion and NASA Plan to Unlock Interplanetary Aerocapture MB edits
articles.description: Using a planet’s atmosphere to secure a satellite’s place in orbit, a process known as “aerocapture”, has been the dream of flight engineers for decades. The only problem? It’s really hard to actually do. It requires control systems, thermal management, and orbital mechanics to all coordinate in a dance that allows a spacecraft to not just slow down while passing by another planet (or moon in some cases) but to start to orbit it without the use of lots of additional propellant. For now, that remains a dream, but a recent NASA contract to a California start-up called Inversion is another step towards making it a reality.
articles.summary: Inversion and NASA collaborate to develop aerocapture technology, enabling spacecraft to use planetary atmospheres for orbital insertion and reducing fuel requirements for interplanetary missions.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter Traces Giant Magnetic Switchbacks Directly Back to the Sun
articles.description: There has been a torrent of solar physics data lately, largely thanks to new spacecraft that have begun actively observing the Sun. One of those spacecraft, Solar Orbiter, happened to have a serendipitous encounter with a type of solar physics phenomenon known as a “switchback”. A new paper, available in Nature Astronomy from researcher Jesse T. Coburn and their co-authors, describes how that serendipitous encounter allowed them to track the switchback back to its birthplace in the solar corona for the first time.
articles.summary: Solar Orbiter traces giant magnetic switchbacks directly to their source on the Sun, advancing understanding of solar magnetic phenomena and solar wind dynamics.

articles.title: Under Extreme Pressure on Ice Giants, Water Ice Gets Weird
articles.description: On Earth, water ice is simply water ice. But under extreme pressure, it takes on an unusual asymmetric form. It stops being molecular and its atoms are forced into a strange asymmetry.
articles.summary: Research reveals that water ice undergoes remarkable transformations under extreme pressure on ice giants, adopting unusual asymmetric crystalline structures.

articles.title: Hubble observations challenge supernova winds' role in cosmic reionization
articles.description: An international team of researchers, including members from the University of Michigan, has revealed surprising results that could rewrite our understanding of a key transition in the early universe.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Hubble observations provide surprising new insights into supernova winds and their role in cosmic reionization, challenging existing models of early universe evolution.

articles.title: Reexamined Viking 2 signal reveals possible marsquake from region active decades later
articles.description: Earthquakes and the seismic waves they generate provide some of the best clues to Earth's interior. To extend that success to other worlds, scientists placed seismometers on the Apollo missions to the moon and on the Viking Mars landers, which reached Mars in 1976. Though the Apollo detectors proved a resounding success, Viking's results on Mars were less clear: Viking 1's seismometer failed to deploy properly, and Viking 2 recorded only two ambiguous events.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Reanalysis of Viking 2 data reveals possible marsquake signatures, demonstrating how seismic studies unlock mysteries of Mars' interior structure.

articles.title: Astronomers uncover the engine behind the most powerful stellar flares in the Kepler field
articles.description: A new study led by researchers at the Konkoly Observatory of the HUN-REN Research Centre for Astronomy and Earth Sciences (HUN-REN CSFK) in Budapest has revealed what makes a distant red giant star the most explosively active in the entire Kepler field—and the answer lies in a surprisingly subtle interplay between a close stellar companion, vast dark starspots and a highly efficient internal magnetic dynamo.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Astronomers identify the engine mechanism behind the most powerful stellar flares observed in the Kepler field, advancing flare prediction and stellar activity understanding.

articles.title: A magnetar can be born when two neutron stars touch
articles.description: All neutron stars have intense magnetic fields. The typical magnetic field of a neutron star is about 100,000 times stronger than the strongest magnetic fields we can create on Earth. But about 1% of neutron stars have even stronger magnetic fields. Known as magnetars, their magnetic fields can be 1,000 times stronger than a regular magnetic field. They are a likely cause of powerful transient events such as soft gamma-ray repeaters and fast radio bursts. A new study looks at how magnetars might form. The findings are published on the arXiv preprint server.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Research reveals that magnetars can form through neutron star mergers, unlocking new understanding of how the universe's most extreme magnetic objects are created.

articles.title: Rare solar radiation storm gives scientists clearest picture yet of flight risks
articles.description: The most comprehensive data set ever collected from Earth's atmosphere during a solar radiation event has highlighted the importance of better-coordinated radiation monitoring for aviation safety, according to new research led by the University of Surrey.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Scientists have gathered the most comprehensive data ever collected during a solar radiation event, providing crucial insights into flight safety risks. This breakthrough dataset advances our understanding of space weather's impact on human spaceflight.
